claims.explanation: Digoxin selectively kills cancer cell lines through inhibition of the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), leading to disruption of ion homeostasis and secondary effects on signaling and metabolism. Sensitivity is likely determined by high expression of ATP1A1 and possibly other ion transporters, while protective features include mutations in ARID1A and KRAS that may confer resistance. The transcriptional similarity to other cardiac glycosides supports on-target activity.

features.basis: Digoxin directly inhibits ATP1A1; higher expression may increase dependence and sensitivity.
ARID1A mutations are enriched in resistant lines, suggesting a role in chromatin remodeling that reduces drug efficacy.
KRAS mutations appear more frequent in resistant lines, possibly due to activation of compensatory survival pathways.
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, though the mechanism is unclear and may reflect genomic instability.
BRAF mutations are observed in several sensitive melanoma lines, but evidence is limited.
PIK3CA mutations appear in some sensitive lines, but also in resistant ones, so this is weak.
NFE2L2 mutations are present in a few sensitive lines, possibly linking oxidative stress response to sensitivity.
PTEN mutations are seen in some sensitive lines, but also in resistant ones, so this is weak.
CDKN2A mutations appear in some sensitive lines, but evidence is not strong.
SMARCA4 mutation in one resistant line suggests possible protection, but limited data.
STK11 mutations appear in some resistant lines, but also in sensitive ones, so weak.
KEAP1 mutations are present in some resistant lines, but also in sensitive ones, so weak.
